successCriteria.description: A new Jest suite exists at tests/unit/shared/port-resolver.test.ts and `npx jest` exits 0 with the whole suite green (the new file is collected by jest.config.js testMatch `**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)` and no pre-existing suite regresses).
Required case 1 (PORT unset): resolvePort(undefined) returns port === DEFAULT_PORT and source === 'DEFAULT'.

Required case 2 (PORT valid): resolvePort('4000') returns port === 4000 with source === 'ENV', AND a whitespace-padded valid value (e.g. ' 4000 ') resolves to port === 4000 with source === 'ENV', proving the trim step of the predicate.
Required case 3 (PORT non-numeric): resolvePort('not-a-number') returns port === DEFAULT_PORT with source === 'DEFAULT'.
Required case 4 (out-of-range): resolvePort('70000') returns port === DEFAULT_PORT with source === 'DEFAULT' — an out-of-range value is INVALID and falls back rather than being passed through.
Strict-predicate cases: each of '3000abc', '3e3', '0xBB8', '+3000', '3000.5', '0', '-1' and '' resolves to port === DEFAULT_PORT with source === 'DEFAULT'.

Diagnostics contract: for every exercised input (valid and invalid, including undefined) the returned ResolvedHttpPort retains rawValue equal to the exact input string as passed (undefined when undefined), and the resolver never throws for any of the listed inputs.
No production source file is modified by this phase: the diff contains only the new test file (src/shared/config/* and src/index.ts are byte-identical to their pre-phase state).

The suite imports PortResolver, DEFAULT_PORT and PortSource from the public entry point '../../../src/shared/config' and contains no bare 3000 literal and no re-implementation of the validity predicate (no local regex/range check used to compute an expected value).

constraints: Exactly one file is created: tests/unit/shared/port-resolver.test.ts. No production source file may be created, modified or deleted in this phase — src/shared/config/* (Phase 1) and src/index.ts (Phase 2) are fixed contracts.

TESTABILITY (BINDING): the test exercises the pure resolver directly. It must NOT mock app.listen, must NOT spawn a child process, and must NOT import src/index.ts to drive the test — it tests the resolver, not the bootstrap, and must not depend on the require.main === module guard.

Imports come only from the public entry point '../../../src/shared/config' (never from './port-resolver' or './port-resolver.interface' directly), matching the module-boundary rule that consumers import through the declared public entry point.
The test must reference DEFAULT_PORT rather than a bare 3000 literal, so the single fallback value stays single (architecture: 'No second literal 3000 may exist anywhere in the codebase').
The test must not re-implement the validity predicate: expectations are asserted against the resolver's output, not computed by a local copy of the trim/regex/range rule.
No test may assert on log output, console.warn, or any warning/error emission on the fallback path — the fallback is SILENT by binding rule (business rule 3).
The suite must not mutate process.env (no setting/restoring PORT) — the resolver takes the raw value as an argument, so environment mutation is unnecessary and would couple the test to global state.

File location and naming follow the existing tests/unit/shared/ convention (date.test.ts, types.test.ts, errors.test.ts, unit-of-work.test.ts) and the suite style of tests/unit/shared/date.test.ts (describe blocks per behaviour, it() with a plain-English assertion).
Strict TypeScript with no implicit any (HARNESS constraint no-any): the test file must typecheck under tsc --noEmit; use unknown/typed values rather than any.
outOfScope: src/shared/config/* (Phase 1: port-resolver.interface.ts, port-resolver.ts, index.ts) — fixed contract, must not be modified.
src/index.ts (Phase 2: bootstrap wiring and the require.main === module guard) — fixed contract, must not be modified or imported by this test.
Any assertion on log output, console.log/console.warn, or the startup log line — the fallback is silent by binding rule.
Integration/e2e coverage of the bootstrap (binding a real socket, app.listen, smoke.js) — this phase is unit-only against the pure resolver.
Migrating DATABASE_URL or JWT_SECRET into src/shared/config (architecture OQ-4) — PORT resolution only in this feature.
Any change to the validity predicate, DEFAULT_PORT value, or the ResolvedHttpPort/PortEnvironmentInput shapes — all fixed by Phase 1 and the reconciled architecture.

ambiguities.description: The architecture's recommended Phase 3 says 'three required cases plus the boundary cases the predicate implies', while PLAN.md Phase 3 mandates four required cases plus eight strict-predicate cases. The phase intent enumerates the four + eight explicitly.
options: Follow the phase intent / PLAN.md: four required cases plus the eight strict-predicate cases (superset, satisfies both)
Follow the architecture's 'three required cases' literally and drop the out-of-range case

ambiguities.description: The architecture's OQ-1 (confirm the strict validity predicate) and OQ-2 (silent fallback vs warning) are recorded as open questions, but the phase intent and PLAN.md treat both as BINDING and already implemented in Phase 1. The test pins the strict predicate and asserts no log output.
options: Treat strict predicate + silent fallback as settled (Phase 1 shipped them; the test pins current behaviour)
Treat them as still open and avoid asserting the strict cases / log silence

ambiguities.description: Whether the suite should assert rawValue retention on the valid ('ENV') path as well as the fallback path. The intent says 'assert rawValue is retained on the returned ResolvedHttpPort for the diagnostics contract' without restricting it to the fallback branch.
options: Assert rawValue on both branches (valid input retains the original untrimmed string; invalid retains the input)
Assert rawValue only on the fallback branch

entityInvariants.invariant: The returned value always carries port (a positive integer in 1..65535 by construction), source ('ENV' when the input was valid, 'DEFAULT' when absent or invalid), and rawValue (the exact input string as passed, undefined when undefined) — rawValue is retained for diagnostics only and is never asserted to be logged.

The snapshot is taken once and never mutated: ABSENT (rawValue === undefined) and PRESENT (rawValue is a string, possibly empty/whitespace/non-numeric/zero/negative/fractional/out-of-range) are terminal observations, not a progression. The test supplies rawValue directly as the resolver argument and must not construct or mutate a snapshot.

Resolution is a pure, total function of its argument: no I/O, no process.env read, no global state, no failure mode — it never throws for any input, including undefined, empty string, and arbitrary non-numeric garbage.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: None — no identity, role or endpoint is involved (GP-005 does not apply).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Total and non-throwing: every input, including undefined and arbitrary non-numeric strings, returns a ResolvedHttpPort. Invalid or absent input yields { port: DEFAULT_PORT, source: 'DEFAULT' } silently — no throw, no warning, no log. Valid input yields { port: n, source: 'ENV' } with n in 1..65535.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Public entry point src/shared/config/index.ts re-exports PortResolver, DEFAULT_PORT, PortSource (plus IPortResolver, PortEnvironmentInput, PortPresence, ResolvedHttpPort)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Importing the entry point has no side effect and throws nothing; the test's only import surface is this module.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Import PortResolver, DEFAULT_PORT and PortSource from the public entry point '../../../src/shared/config' — never from port-resolver.ts or port-resolver.interface.ts directly — matching the module-boundary rule that consumers import only through the declared public entry point.

Assert the fallback against the exported DEFAULT_PORT constant rather than a bare 3000 literal, so the single fallback value stays single (architecture: 'No second literal 3000 may exist anywhere in the codebase').
Match the existing shared-unit-test suite style and location convention: describe blocks per behaviour with plain-English it() assertions, as in the sibling shared suites.
The expected source discriminator values must be the canonical PortSource members 'ENV' and 'DEFAULT' — no other spelling or a locally re-declared union.
The test file must be collected by the existing Jest configuration (testMatch '**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)', ts-jest preset, node environment) without any jest.config change.

The asserted behaviour must match the binding business rules of the reconciled PORT feature: strict predicate (trim, /^[0-9]+$/, 1..65535), silent fallback to DEFAULT_PORT, and rawValue retained for diagnostics only (never logged).

integrationPoints.why: The only import surface for the suite; supplies PortResolver, DEFAULT_PORT and PortSource.
Owns the canonical validity predicate and DEFAULT_PORT that the assertions pin; read-only, never modified.
Style and location reference for the new sibling suite.
Collects the new file via testMatch; no config change permitted.
The consumer of the resolver in production (Phase 2). Referenced only to confirm the test does NOT import it — no coupling.
